sources.title: Daniel Harlow, The Ryu-Takayanagi Formula from Quantum Error Correction, complete paper
sources.locator: Complete 62-page paper retrieved. Inspected Appendix A.7.2–A.7.3, PDF pp. 52–54, especially Eqs. (A.6)–(A.10) and (A.19)–(A.22).
sources.reading_extent: The complete paper was retrieved. The finite-dimensional block decomposition, the code-state form with maximally mixed ancillary factors, and the algebraic entropy/relative-entropy decompositions in Appendix A.7.2–A.7.3 were inspected. Only these specified sections are claimed as read.

contents.name: Appendix A.7.2, Eqs. (A.6)–(A.9), finite direct-sum sector representation

source_review.read_extent: Read the finite-dimensional direct-sum decomposition and the block-diagonal representative state with sector probabilities and a maximally mixed ancillary factor.
source_review.supports: Provides a holography/QEC treatment of the finite sector structure motivating the model definition.
source_review.limitations: Harlow's displayed ancillary factors are maximally mixed. The local definition allows any fixed faithful ancillary density matrix and makes no holographic identification.

contents.name: Appendix A.7.2–A.7.3, Eqs. (A.10), (A.19)–(A.22), sector entropy and relative entropy

source_review.read_extent: Read the entropy decomposition into a central Shannon term and block entropy, and the relative-entropy decomposition into the classical sector term and weighted within-sector terms.
source_review.supports: Independently treats the finite sector entropy and relative-entropy structure used by the proposition.
source_review.limitations: The local proposition proves its stated finite matrix formula for arbitrary fixed faithful ancillary matrices. Harlow's paper does not justify a universal area law, continuum limit, or literal black-hole interpretation here.

contents.name: Appendix A.7.3, central Shannon entropy and finite sector specialization

source_review.read_extent: Read the finite classical center contribution and its addition to within-sector entropy.
source_review.supports: Supports separating the central sector-probability term from ancillary and logical entropy contributions.
source_review.limitations: The specific one-dimensional and maximally mixed two-sector ancillas are evaluated locally; no geometric area is asserted.

sources.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, complete author-hosted book manuscript
sources.locator: Complete 598-page manuscript retrieved. Inspected §5.2.1 for finite-dimensional entropy and quantum relative entropy conventions and §5.2.2, PDF pp. 268–269, Propositions 5.20–5.21 and Eqs. (5.94)–(5.99).
sources.reading_extent: The full manuscript was retrieved. The finite spectral entropy and relative-entropy definitions and the direct-sum/tensor-product entropy formulas and tensor-product relative-entropy identity were inspected. Watrous's entropy/relative-entropy logarithm convention is base two; the local results use natural logarithms, multiplying all corresponding terms by ln(2).

source_review.limitations: The local definition fixes the natural-log nats convention from its current mathematical supplier and does not import a holographic interpretation.

source_review.supports: Corroborates the direct block and tensor eigenvalue calculation in the proposition.
source_review.limitations: The proposition supplies its own complete proof and explicitly treats possibly singular logical density matrices using 0 log 0 = 0.

source_review.limitations: The local proof does not take this citation as a proof of the full direct-sum formula; it derives the sector weights and central classical term explicitly.
